newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-INDONESIA AND KUWAIT DRAW 2-2 IN ASIAN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INDONESIA AND KUWAIT DRAW 2-2 IN ASIAN CUP.

text.p: Kuwait scored two late goals to earn a 2-2 draw against Indonesia on Wednesday in a Group A match of the Asian Cup.

Defender Yousif al-Dakhi scored from the penalty spot in the 84th minute to level the tie after Indonesian defender Aples Tecuari floored substitute Khaled Fairouz inside the penalty box only four minutes after he came on.
Eleven minutes earlier striker Hani Saqer had given Kuwait a lifeline at a time when the Indonesian defence had looked capable of holding on to their two-goal advantage
Indonesia stunned Kuwait, who had much of the play early on, with a superbly taken goal after 20 minutes.
Widodo Purta rose acrobatically from 15 meters out to meet a cross by Ronny Wabia from the right flank, firing a powerful overhead kick into the top corner.
Kuwait piled on the pressure after the goal with Bashar al-Halabeej and Esam Sakeen missing open goals in the 24th and 29th minutes respectively.
But Indonesia looked dangerous on the break and man of the match Purta came close with a fierce shot from just outside the penalty area before Wabia put his side 2-0 up in the 41st minute.
He pounced on a loose ball just inside the area after a swift counter-attack saw Kuwait keeper Khaled al-Fadhli parry away a shot by Purata.

Indonesia defended well for most of the second half, restricting the Kuwaiti forwards to trying their luck from long range until the 73rd minute when Saqer tucked the ball in after it rebounded off the post.
Saqer came close five minutes later when he saw another close-range shot cleared off the line by Marzuki Badriawan.
Indonesian keeper Kurinia Sandi was stretchered off in the 79th minute after a collision with a Kuwaiti player. The substitute keeper was helpless when Dahli scored the penalty.

Kuwait: 1-Khaled al-Fadhli, 2-Osama Abdullah, 4-Yousif al-Dakhi, 6-Wail al-Habashi, 7-Bader al-Halabeej, 9-Bashar Abdulaziz, 11-Abdullah Seehan (18-Waleed Mubarak 60th), 12-Fawaz Al-Ahmad, 17-Esam Sakeen, 19-Hani Saqer, 20-Jassem Al-Houwaid (10-Khaled Fairouz 80th).

Indonesia: 1-Kurnia Sandi (20-Hendro Kartiko 79th), 2-Agung Setyabudi, 4-Yeyen Tumera, 5-Aples Tecuari, 6-Sudiriman, 7-Widodo Gahyo Purata, 8-Ronny Wabia, 11-Bima Sakti, 12-Chris Yarangga, 16-Marzuki Badriawan, 18-Supriyono (3-Suwandi Siwoyo 55th).
